title: Both clefs from memory
prompt: Without looking, write the notes on the **lines** and in the **spaces** of the treble clef and the bass clef, bottom to top. Then name the two pairs of neighbouring white keys that are a half step apart.
hints: Treble lines: Every Good Boy Deserves Fruit.
Bass spaces: All Cows Eat Grass.
starter:
Treble lines:
Treble spaces:
Bass lines:
Bass spaces:
Half-step pairs:
solution:
Treble lines: E G B D F
Treble spaces: F A C E
Bass lines: G B D F A
Bass spaces: A C E G
Half-step pairs: E–F and B–C

title: Counting beats
prompt: In quarter-note beats, write the length of: a whole note, a half note, a dotted half note, a dotted quarter note, an eighth note, and a sixteenth note. Then write how many beats per bar, and which note gets the beat, in 3/4 and in 6/8.
hints: Each value halves the one before.
A dot adds half the note's own value.
solution:
Whole 4, half 2, dotted half 3, dotted quarter 1.5, eighth 0.5, sixteenth 0.25.
3/4: three beats, each a quarter note.
6/8: two beats, each a dotted quarter (three eighths).

title: Major scales and signatures
prompt: From memory: write the order of sharps and the order of flats. Then spell the major scales of **A**, **E♭** and **B**, and give how many sharps or flats each has.
hints: Pattern W W H W W W H, each letter once.
Sharps: Father Charles Goes Down And Ends Battle.
solution:
Order of sharps: F C G D A E B. Order of flats: B E A D G C F.
A major: A B C♯ D E F♯ G♯ (3 sharps).
E♭ major: E♭ F G A♭ B♭ C D (3 flats).
B major: B C♯ D♯ E F♯ G♯ A♯ (5 sharps).

title: Intervals by half steps
prompt: Write the half-step count of each interval: m2, M2, m3, M3, P4, tritone, P5, m6, M6, m7, M7, P8. Then name these intervals: C–A♭, D–F♯, G–F.
hints: P5 is 7 half steps; work outwards from there.
Count letters first for the names.
solution:
m2 1, M2 2, m3 3, M3 4, P4 5, tritone 6, P5 7, m6 8, M6 9, m7 10, M7 11, P8 12.
C–A♭: minor sixth. D–F♯: major third. G–F: minor seventh.

title: The triads of a key
prompt: Write the Roman-numeral pattern of the triads in a major key. Then spell all seven triads of **G major** with their chord symbols.
hints: Major, minor, minor, major, major, minor, diminished.
G major has one sharp: F♯.
solution:
I ii iii IV V vi vii°.
G major: G (G B D), Am (A C E), Bm (B D F♯), C (C E G), D (D F♯ A), Em (E G B), F♯° (F♯ A C).

title: Cadences and progressions
prompt: Name the four cadences with their chords. Then write I–IV–V–I and I–V–vi–IV in **D major** as chord symbols.
hints: D major: D E F♯ G A B C♯.
solution:
Authentic V–I, plagal IV–I, half (any chord)–V, deceptive V–vi.
D major I–IV–V–I: D G A D. I–V–vi–IV: D A Bm G.
